title: GET /api/orders/{orderId} returns any user's order (no ownership check)
owner_hint: component: src/Ordering.API/; no CODEOWNERS; recent committers Rob Conery, David Fowler (1/4 each)
rationale: Root cause OrderQueries.cs:8-10: GetOrderAsync selects by primary key only, and its sole caller OrdersApi.GetOrderAsync (OrdersApi.cs:84) never reads caller identity. IOrderQueries.GetOrderAsync now takes userId and filters o.Id == id && o.Buyer.IdentityGuid == userId (same predicate as GetOrdersFromUserAsync, OrderQueries.cs:40); OrdersApi passes IdentityService.GetUserIdentity() (sub). Non-owned orders throw KeyNotFoundException -> existing 404, so no exists-but-not-yours oracle. Null/empty userId rejected in the query to avoid EF IS NULL matching buyer-less rows. No admin bypass added. Agent ran `git apply --check` from stdin (no writes) against the read-only brief.
variants_checked: GetOrdersFromUserAsync already filtered; GetCardTypesAsync reference data; only production caller OrdersApi.GetOrderAsync updated plus two test mocks; cancel (f002), ship (f011), create/draft (f005) left to siblings; mobile-bff /api/orders/{*any} reaches the same handler; functional test GetStoredOrdersWithOrderId still expects 404.
bypass_considered: Sequential id enumeration via API or BFF now 404s; principal without sub hits the IsNullOrEmpty guard; identity comes only from the token, never request input; no other order-detail read path exists.
test_note: tests/Ordering.UnitTests/Application/OrdersWebApiTest.cs Get_order_of_another_user_returns_not_found; two existing mocks updated for the new signature. SQL predicate not unit-tested (no EF in-memory provider in Ordering.UnitTests). Not built or run.
review_reason: The OrderQueries.cs hunk changes the lookup to FirstOrDefaultAsync(o => o.Id == id && o.Buyer.IdentityGuid == userId) and OrdersApi.cs:84 passes IdentityService.GetUserIdentity(), closing the IDOR at the data layer with the same ownership predicate GetOrdersFromUserAsync uses; empty identity fails closed and no new input is trusted. Style 5 because the OrdersApi.cs hunk header was off by one (-80,6 should be -80,7 +80,8) and the OrderQueries.cs blank context line lacked the source's trailing whitespace. Orchestrator corrected both mechanical issues in PATCHES/bug_00/patch.diff after review; content unchanged. The new unit test mocks the query layer, so the EF filter itself is not exercised.
